items.title: Students want say in law replacing AUKU
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Student leaders have welcomed the government's decision to repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU), but want students to have a meaningful say in drafting the legislation that replaces it. Universiti Malaya student representative Syam Eddy Ahmad, a second-year Environmental Studies student, described the repeal as a long-awaited victory for the student movement, saying AUKU had historically restricted student autonomy and academic freedom. "Students themselves must be involved in drafting it, together with academics and universities," he said.

items.title: Afternoon checks show nine Sarawak areas with unhealthy air quality, Serian still very unhealthy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Air Pollution Index (API) reading at Serian station in Sarawak reached 227 (very unhealthy) as of 2pm today, while nine other areas in the state recorded unhealthy readings. She said air quality nationwide had deteriorated today, with an increase in areas recording unhealthy API readings in Sarawak due to haze moving in from various directions. “The National Open Burning Action Plan and the National Haze Action Plan have been activated to coordinate action among government agencies in addressing open burning and dealing with the national haze situation,” she said.

items.title: Police arrest 5, seize RM12.8mil in two smuggling operations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested five people and seized contraband and other goods worth RM12.8 million in two operations targeting suspected smuggling in Kuala Lumpur and Klang. "Among the items seized were 112 cans and 3,696 bottles of various brands of liquor worth about RM2.57 million, as well as 4,092 bottles of liquor worth about RM2.7 million. He said the seizure included Chinese liquor worth RM2.1 million, 245 cartons of white cigarettes, or 49,000 sticks, worth nearly RM300,000, and 1,800 helmets worth RM1.8 million.

items.title: Muhyiddin trial: Witness says MOF wanted open tender, but PMO insisted on pre-qualification
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Finance Ministry (MOF) had initially wanted government projects under the Bumiputera contractors' programme Jana Wibawa to be carried out through open tender, but the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) had instructed for Jana Wibawa projects to be given out either by direct negotiation or through a pre-qualification tender, a senior MOF officer said today. At the time of the Jana Wibawa programme during Muhyiddin's administration, Rosni was the deputy under secretary of the same division and also chaired a Finance Ministry committee that evaluated whether proposed contractors forwarded by the PMO were qualified to be given Jana Wibawa projects. "Initially, Jana Wibawa, we wanted to carry out through open tender, but we received instructions from PMO.

items.title: Indonesia rejects US claim over transshipment of Chinese goods
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia denied a recent US report claiming its involvement in the transshipment of goods, the country's senior economic minister Airlangga Hartarto said in a statement on Thursday. Below are the details: Airlangga was referring to a report released by Washington, which claimed the US is losing some US$19 billion to US$26 billion in annual tariff revenue to goods, largely from China, that are transshipped through third countries, including Indonesia, to avoid US import duties. "Indonesia has been accused, along with Brazil, Malaysia, Thailand, Turkiye, and Vietnam, of being part of a global transshipment network.

items.title: Rapid KL to run trains, selected buses 24 hours for National Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rapid KL will extend the operating hours of its rail and selected bus services to 24 hours from Aug 30 to 31 to support National Day 2026 celebrations. "Aimed at easing public movement during the Merdeka period, the move will cover all rail services, including the Light Rail Transit (LRT), Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and Kuala Lumpur Monorail. The Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Sunway Line, several bus routes and the Rapid KL On-Demand (ROD) service will similarly operate around the clock.

items.title: Melaka polls: PN ready to forgo BN cooperation if it chooses PH, says Hadi
items.summary: MARANG: Perikatan Nasional is prepared to forego cooperation with Barisan Nasional in the Melaka state election if the latter chooses to work with Pakatan Harapan. Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said that while the PN coalition was confident it could pursue alternative strategies, discussions were still ongoing among its leaders, particularly on cooperation with BN for the Melaka state election. He said no final decision had been made, although a majority of BN leaders were understood to favour continuing cooperation with PN.

items.title: Security guard jailed 8 years, caned twice for sexually assaulting 10-year-old boy
items.summary: MUAR: A security guard was sentenced to eight years in prison and two strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court here today for physically sexually assaulting a 10-year-old boy at a resource centre last month. Police investigations found that the victim and the accused knew each other and often played games on their mobile phones at the resource centre. While at the resource centre, the accused pulled down the victim's trousers and removed them.

items.title: LYC Healthcare aims Aug 28 release of delayed annual report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: LYC Healthcare Bhd is targeting Aug 28 to issue its delayed annual report for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26), as outstanding audit matters involving a disposed subsidiary and accounting treatments remain unresolved. SBY Partners has tentatively targeted board approval of the financial statements on or before Aug 28, subject to LYC management's full cooperation in resolving the outstanding matters. On Aug 5, SBY Partners informed LYC's board and management that the financial statements were still under review and expected to finalise them by Aug 10.

items.title: MOH bans three batches of Chomel hand sanitiser over excessive methanol content
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has banned the sale of Chomel Hand Sanitizer after three batches of the product were found to contain methanol above the permitted limit. As such, the MOH urged the public not to purchase or use products from the affected batches. “Uncontrolled exposure to methanol can pose serious health risks.

items.title: Police arrest drug suspect after struggle with machete leaves officer injured in Jeli
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 21 — A suspect believed to be involved in drug trafficking was arrested after brandishing a machete at police officers and injuring one during a raid in Kampung Lubok Bongor, Jeli, yesterday. Jeli police chief Supt Kamarulzaman Harun said the 11am incident took place when a team from the district police Criminal Investigation Division raided an unnumbered house in the village. “The suspect acted aggressively by pulling out a machete tucked at his waist and brandishing it at the police officers while threatening to kill.

items.title: Haze worsens in Sarawak as unhealthy API readings rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality nationwide has worsened, with more areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as haze from various directions moves into the state. In a statement today, the department said one area recorded very unhealthy air quality while nine recorded unhealthy levels, all in Sarawak. Another 56 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings, while two recorded good levels.

items.title: Singaporean security guard jailed 14 days, fined RM7,000 for insulting Islam
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A Singaporean security guard was sentenced to 14 days in jail and fined RM7,000 by the magistrates' court here today after pleading guilty to insulting Islam last month. Magistrate A. Shaarmini ordered Mohamed Anim Atam, 56, to serve the jail term from the date of his arrest on Tuesday. The court also ordered him to serve an additional three months in jail if he failed to pay the fine.

items.title: Six charged with kidnapping Singaporean man for S$20,000 ransom in Johor
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 21 — Six individuals including a woman pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to a charge of kidnapping a Singaporean man, 32, for the purpose of obtaining a ransom of S$20,000 (RM63,000), earlier this month. M. Balamurugan, 46, K. Saravanan, 40, P. Sri Devi, 41, G. Puganeswaran, 38, S. Gobinath, 38, and X. Adwin Nicholas, 41, made the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Nor Aziati Jaafar. The charges were brought under Section 3 of the Kidnapping Act 1961 and read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for a prison sentence of up to 40 years and whipping, if convicted.

items.title: Two Malaysians held in Thailand with 1,560 Epam tablets
items.summary: SUNGAI GOLOK: Two Malaysians were arrested by Thai police after they were allegedly found in possession of 1,560 Epam tablets in Sungai Golok last night. Sungai Golok police chief Police Colonel Than Sirikhan said the two men, aged 24 and 30, were detained at about 10.30pm along Anukachart Usorn Road. He said the arrests were carried out by personnel from the Sungai Golok police station's Rapid Response Unit and Wihok Network Unit in front of Ban Boss Restaurant.

items.title: [UPDATED] 10 GOF personnel arrested over alleged Penang e-waste factory extortion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ten General Operations Force (GOF) personnel have been arrested to assist in investigations following an extortion case involving an e-waste processing factory in Tasek Gelugor, Penang. The incident occurred on Wednesday, Federal police Internal Security and Public Order (Operations) deputy director Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim said. Also present were Federal Police Internal Security and Public Order Department (GOF) deputy director Datuk Mohamad Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi and Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar.

items.title: Malaysian airports see 9.3pct jump in international traffic
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: International traffic across Malaysian airports rose 9.3 per cent month-on-month to 4.5 million movements in July. Overall passenger movements across the airports in Malaysia were 11 per cent lower year-on-year (YoY) in July. International traffic grew 6.1 per cent YoY during the period, while domestic traffic dropped 6.7 per cent.

items.title: Ex-Pakistan PM Imran Khan returned to jail after medical checkup
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was returned to jail after a medical examination at a health facility in the capital, Islamabad, following court orders, a senior official said Friday, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported. Without naming Khan, 73, Pakistani Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said: "In the light of the Supreme Court's decision, the prisoner (Imran Khan) was taken to the hospital under appropriate security arrangements during the intervening night of August 20 and 21, 2026." He added that Khan's sister, Uzma Khan, "remained present throughout all stages of the medical examination/treatment."

items.title: High Court proceeds with Duta Enclave assessment as Semantan Estate weighs secret settlement terms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Putrajaya’s offer to compensate Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd without a formal assessment exercise remains open, though the company has yet to provide a response, according to a senior federal counsel. Last week, Semantan applied to postpone the hearing to evaluate the government’s proposal, but Justice Roslan Mat Nor rejected the application, allowing the assessment of compensation to proceed. The appeals court also mandated an assessment of mesne profits — compensation for the loss of use of the property.

items.title: MMHE Q2 earnings jump six-fold on heavy engineering boost
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Marine and Heavy Engineering Holdings Bhd (MMHE) posted a stronger net profit in the second quarter of financial year 2026 (Q2 FY26), driven by a higher contribution from its heavy engineering segment. Net profit jumped more than six-fold to RM60.59 million from RM10 million a year earlier, while revenue surged 128.6 per cent to RM986.7 million from RM431.57 million. For the first half of FY26, net profit rose to RM74.9 million from RM22 million a year earlier, while revenue increased 70 per cent to RM1.5 billion from RM884.7 million.

items.title: Penang tightens short-term rental rules, gives operators 2 month to register
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang has introduced new licensing rules for short-term rentals, giving operators a two-month grace period to register before enforcement begins. The new Private Short-term Accommodation (Local Authorities of Penang) By-laws 2026 came into force on Aug 1, giving local councils clearer powers to regulate short-term accommodation, including Airbnb-type operations. The new by-laws require private accommodation operators to obtain a licence from the relevant local authority and comply with requirements covering operations, cleanliness, safety, prohibited activities and public nuisance.

items.title: Six charged with kidnapping Singaporean man for RM63,000 ransom
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU: Six people, including a woman, pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to kidnapping a Singaporean man and demanding RM63,000 in ransom earlier this month. M. Balamurugam, 46, K. Saravanan, 40, P. Sri Devi, 41, G. Puganeswaran, 38, S. Gobinath, 38, and X. Adwin Nicholas, 41, entered the pleas after the charges were read before Judge Nor Aziati Jaafar. They were charged under Section 3 of the Kidnapping Act 1961, read with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of up to 40 years and whipping upon conviction.

items.title: Perak stands firm on vape sales ban despite court challenge
items.summary: State Human Resources, Health, Indian Community Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the parties had filed a judicial review application against the state government at the Ipoh High Court on March 18. He said the challenge appeared to question whether the state government had acted beyond the powers or jurisdiction conferred by law. Sivanesan said the state government's decision was based on the Local Government Act 1976, which empowers local authorities to decide whether to issue business licences for specific purposes.

items.title: Govt challenges Duta Enclave land valuation
items.summary: Nurhafizza questioned Foo on several comparable transactions involving bungalow lots in Bukit Tunku, which the witness had used to assess the 1956 market value of the 263.272-acre subject property. Foo disagreed. Foo disagreed.

items.title: Anwar asks Indonesia’s Prabowo to intercede in Felda's RM2.5b PT Eagle High loss
items.summary: BANGI, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has reached out formally to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, requesting special intervention regarding Felda’s investments in Indonesia, specifically involving PT Eagle High Plantations Tbk (EHP). This is one example,” Anwar said. The PM disclosed these details during a Friendly Session with Felda’s top management and managers today.

items.title: Operational excellence key to Asean's energy transition – TNB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Operational excellence must go beyond cost efficiency to strengthen grid resilience, enhance real-time system visibility and support the safe and reliable integration of renewable energy as Asean's energy landscape continues to evolve. Speaking at the 3rd Asean Operational Excellence Summit 2026 (OPEX 2026), Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) chief strategy and ventures officer Dr Mohd Fadzil Mohd Siamhe said the increasing interconnection of power systems and accelerating energy transition require utilities to build greater agility in responding to a rapidly changing operating environment. "Operational excellence must go beyond cost efficiency.

items.title: Velesto profit drops in Q2, but says outlook brightens
items.summary: Velesto's net profit for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 fell to RM531,000 from RM50.44 million a year earlier, mainly due to lower rig utilisation and daily charter rates. Velesto said its drilling services segment recorded a lower revenue of RM149.5 million for the current quarter, compared to RM195.8 million a year ago. For the cumulative six months, the company's earnings dropped 72.5 per cent YoY to RM28.39 million from RM103.04 million last year while revenue dropped to 337.38 million from RM424.56 million.

items.title: Filipino woman jailed 5 months for MyKad offence
items.summary: Lorna Adilun was sentenced by magistrate Ellyna Othman at the magistrate's court here today. The shop assistant was charged with deliberately providing false information when applying for a replacement identity card under the identity of another person at the National Registration Department (NRD) branch at the Pahang Urban Transformation Centre at 4.19pm on June 9. According to the case facts, Lorna used the identity of a person known as Zuriah when applying for the replacement MyKad.

items.title: Anwar: Action against Tabung Haji, Felda based on wrongdoing, not religion or race
items.summary: KAJANG, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has rejected claims that the government’s scrutiny of Tabung Haji (TH) is driven by the institution’s Islamic identity, insisting that any action taken is a response to mismanagement and wrongdoing, not religious or racial targeting. Speaking at a programme with Felda’s top management today, Anwar said the same principle applied across the board, citing Felda as another example of an institution closely associated with the Malay community that has faced government intervention over past failures, FMT reported. “Some Islamic party leaders say action is mainly being taken against Malay-Muslim agencies.

items.title: Family seeks answers over Kepong petrol attack after suspect's arrest
items.summary: The victim's daughter, Yap, said the family was relieved following the suspect's arrest but remained frustrated that they had yet to receive an official explanation from police about what led to the attack. Police have said the incident was believed to have stemmed from a personal grudge. Yap, who is the fourth of five siblings in a single-parent family, said the family was particularly concerned about police describing the 59-year-old suspect and her 62-year-old mother as acquaintances.

items.title: Myanmar military offensive targets land for Russia-backed port project
items.summary: MYANMAR'S military has deployed hundreds of troops to forcibly clear areas marked for a Russia-backed special economic zone in the country's south, burning villages and sealing off surrounding tracts of land, according to resistance fighters and a local activist with direct knowledge. The offensive around the Dawei Special Economic Zone (SEZ) — that includes a planned deep-sea port and power plant on the Andaman Sea — is the clearest sign yet that Myanmar's military-backed government is willing to use force to revive a project touted as a strategic alternative to the Strait of Malacca. Since July, the military has pumped hundreds of soldiers into the southern Tanintharyi Region, bordering Thailand, where Dawei is located, sparking battles with local resistance groups who have been forced to retreat, according to two sources.

items.title: Pig farm in Perak told to halt expansion works pending approval
items.summary: IPOH: A pig farm operator in Kampung Perlop 1, Sungai Siput, has been told to stop expansion works after carrying out land levelling while its application for planning permission is still being processed. State Human Resources, Health, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the operator had breached procedures by carrying out construction-related works before obtaining approval from the local authority. He said the farm was in the process of being converted from a conventional operation into a modern, fully enclosed pig farming facility.

items.title: Government agency chairman among five remanded in MACC probe over alleged below-market land sale
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 21 — The Magistrate’s Court here today granted a four-day remand order for five individuals, including the chairman of a government agency with the title of Datuk, to assist in an investigation into suspected abuse of position involving the disposal of land. Magistrate Noor Idayu Salim issued the remand order following an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests when contacted yesterday, saying the case was being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Penang Hill cable car hits 32pc completion; operations expected by late 2027
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 21 — The Penang Hill cable car project has reached 32 per cent completion and is expected to be physically finished by August next year, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. Speaking during a monitoring visit from the Botanic Gardens to the summit of Penang Hill, Chow noted that the project has entered a more promising phase following the completion of all underground works. “We expect the work to progress faster because above-ground construction is easier to control compared with underground works,” Chow said.

items.title: Felda task force to examine current management, not just past problems, says Anwar
items.summary: BANGI, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would wait for the complete report of the Special Task Force investigating the management of the Federal Land Development Authority (FELDA) before making any official announcement. He said the special task force had begun its work and the findings of the investigation were expected to be presented in the near future. “(Its aspects include) all matters regarding management, improving management... of course identifying past problems, but what is important is current management and way forward,” he said.

items.title: Anwar says Felda task force has begun work
items.summary: BANGI: A special task force investigating issues involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) has begun its work, with its findings expected to be announced once the investigations are completed, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the task force would conduct a broad review covering past problems, improvements to management and measures needed to strengthen Felda moving forward. Asked about the scope of the task force, Anwar said it would examine all relevant aspects, including previous shortcomings as well as Felda's current management and future direction.

items.title: Singaporean man jailed for insulting Islam during e-hailing trip in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 21 — A 56-year-old Singaporean man has been jailed for 14 days and fined RM7,000 after admitting to demeaning Islam during a trip in Johor Bahru last month. Mohamed Anim Atam pleaded guilty to the charges before Magistrate A. Shaarmini. The incident occurred at approximately 5pm on July 30, as the accused travelled from Jalan Tun Razak to Jalan Meldrum.

items.title: Gambling, traffic and permit issues raise concerns in Bukit Bintang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Illegal gambling, traffic congestion and foreigners working or operating businesses without valid permits are among the main complaints in Bukit Bintang, prompting calls for more "drastic" enforcement. Keadilan Bukit Bintang Public Complaints Bureau chairman Tengku Imran Tengku Zainal Abidin said these issues were tarnishing the image of the capital's premier tourism and commercial hub. Action must involve both enforcement and welfare agencies," he said.

items.title: Genting shares fall 6pct after Q2 earnings miss expectations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Bhd's share price fell nearly six per cent after its second-quarter (Q2) earnings fell short of analysts' expectations. Year-to-date, Genting's shares have fallen 87 sen, or 29.2 per cent, from RM2.98. Public Investment Bank Bhd analyst Eltricia Foong said the performances of both Genting and Genting Malaysia came in well below expectations.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar seeks Prabowo's help over Felda Eagle High investment
items.summary: BANGI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has written to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto seeking his assistance in looking into issues surrounding the Federal Land Development Authority's (Felda) investment in Eagle High Plantations. This is one example," he said during an engagement session with Felda's top management and managers here today. Present was Felda director-general Datuk Dr Suzana Idayu Wati Osman.

items.title: Airbnb crackdown: Penang introduces new licensing laws for short-term rentals
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 20 — Penang has introduced a new regulatory framework to govern short-term rentals of private accommodations, including Airbnbs and homestays, effective August 1. State local government and town and country planning committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye announced that the Penang Private Short-term Accommodation By-Laws 2026 now require all TIP operators to obtain official licences from their respective city councils. Previously, local authorities lacked the legal teeth to take action against unlicensed operators.

items.title: Kossan earnings forecast trimmed amid higher costs, falling prices
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Analysts have cut their target prices for Kossan Rubber Industries Bhd after revising down their earnings forecasts for the glovemaker. HLIB lowered its financial year 2026 (FY26) earnings forecast by 11.0 per cent. The firm said Kossan's glove and clean-room segment is expected to post weaker quarter-on-quarter earnings in Q3 FY26.

items.title: Police escorts should protect, not privilege, says criminologist
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Police escorts and emergency signals for VIPs must be based on necessity and public interest, not status, says senior criminologist Datuk Dr P. Sundramoorthy. Bukit Aman Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said flashing beacon lights and sirens did not give enforcement or emergency vehicle drivers carte blanche to run red lights . "Rank alone should not create an automatic entitlement to emergency traffic privileges," he said.

items.title: Malaysia targets first ‘made by Malaysia’ chips using Arm Limited technology by 2030, says economy minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — The government is targeting 2030 for the first “Made by Malaysia” chips developed using Arm Limited technology to enter production and the semiconductor supply chain. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said four companies have so far begun designing chips using technology from British semiconductor technology company Arm Limited, with the aim of eventually bringing their products into production and the semiconductor supply chain. Akmal said eight Arm technology-access packages — comprising four Arm CSS and four Arm Flexible Access tokens — had so far been offered to five local companies.

items.title: Tiktoker under police probe after allegedly stepping on Sarawak flag
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 21 — A TikToker is being investigated after uploading a video showing a man allegedly disrespecting Sarawak by deliberately stepping on the Ibu Pertiwi flag. Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the district police headquarters has received two reports regarding the incident. The TikToker allegedly uploaded similar content previously before deleting it several hours later.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji CEO remanded seven days in MACC probe linked to RCI findings
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chief executive officer has reportedly been remanded for seven days to assist an investigation stemming from the findings of the royal commission of inquiry (RCI) into the pilgrims’ fund. Berita Harian reported that Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah issued the remand order, which runs until August 27, after allowing an application by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) at the Putrajaya Magistrates’ Court this morning. Separately, Malay Mail reported on August 15 that MACC had detained seven people in investigations arising from the RCI report, comprising a shipping company CEO, two company directors and four former members of TH’s senior management.

items.title: Putrajaya gears up for National Day bash, expects 80,000 visitors
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — More than 80,000 visitors are expected to flood Dataran Putrajaya in conjunction with National Day 2026, with preparations now reaching between 85 and 90 per cent. Ministry of Communications secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah said preparations involving various levels, including static training of all contingents, had begun in preparation for the celebration themed “Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati”. Also present were PPj president Datuk Mohd Sakeri Abdul Kadir and chief ceremonial officer of the Government Ceremony and Secretariat Division of the International Conference Datuk Rozainor Ramli.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI probe: Former CEO arrives in Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court for remand
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — A former chief executive officer of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has arrived at the Magistrate’s Court here for remand proceedings related to investigations into a case linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on TH. The man, in his 60s, arrived at 9.35 am wearing an orange Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) remand shirt. The RCI report, which investigated issues concerning TH’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020, also listed problematic investments that require a forensic audit.

items.title: GOF raids seven illegal sand mining sites across three states, seizes RM13m worth of assets
items.summary: GOF Central Brigade commander SAC Hakemal Hawari said the operation to crack down on the activities began at 11am yesterday, covering the areas of Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Johor. Meanwhile, Hakemal said the latest raid at 3.30pm yesterday targeted an illegal operation site covering an area of 0.647 hectares at Lot PT 89, Jalan Lapangan Terbang Subang Lama, which is believed to be processing sand without permission. “The operation team also seized 1,500 tonnes of sand, heavy machinery and sand washing and processing equipment with an estimated value of RM5 million at this location alone,” he said after visiting the illegal site after the raid here last night.

items.title: Dengue cases surge 56pc as MOH warns of nationwide spread
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has sounded the alarm over a significant surge in dengue cases across Malaysia, with infections spiking by more than 50 per cent compared to last year. Health officials attribute this rise to Malaysia's current volatile weather patterns. The ministry stressed that dengue control is a collective responsibility, particularly as more than 70 per cent of Aedes breeding sites are still located within residential premises.

items.title: Any lane, any time: Plus activates JustGo ANPR toll payments across North-South Expressway minus Penang Bridge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Plus Malaysia has activated its JustGo toll payment system across the entire North-South Expressway (NSE) network, except the Penang Bridge, using automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) to allow motorists to pay tolls through any available lane. Under the JustGo framework, a registered vehicle’s plate number anchors the payment process. To activate the service, motorists must download the JustGo app on Android or iOS and register their vehicle plate number.

items.title: Anwar impressed by Sukma’s young athletes, hopes to see them represent country
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim hopes the young athletes competing in the 2026 Selangor Malaysia Games (Sukma) will go on to represent Malaysia on the international stage. “Hopefully, they will one day have the opportunity to represent Malaysia and make the country proud on the international stage,” he said. Selangor is hosting the biennial games again after 28 years, with more than 5,000 young athletes from across the country competing for 468 gold medals in 37 sports until August 24.

items.title: Two cyclists die in Putrajaya after vehicle hits them while changing lanes, say police
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 21 — Two cyclists died after being hit by a vehicle at kilometre 9.0 of Jalan Persiaran Selatan, Putrajaya, last night, said Putrajaya district police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed. In a statement today, Aidi Sham said the accident occurred at 10.15pm, involving a vehicle driven by a local man in his 40s and two male cyclists aged in their 40s and 30s respectively. “Initial investigations found that the vehicle being driven had changed direction from the middle lane to the left lane before hitting the two cyclists.

items.title: Police hunt suspects after attempted armed robbery of Klang gold shop leaves one injured
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 21 — Police are hunting for suspects believed to be involved in an attempted robbery of a gold shop at Jalan Tengku Kelana, Klang, near here, yesterday morning, which has gone viral on social media. Klang Selatan district deputy police chief Supt Kamalariffin Aman Shah confirmed the incident. “Klang Selatan district police headquarters (IPD) Criminal Investigation Division has opened an investigation paper under Section 394 of the Penal Code for causing hurt during an attempted gang robbery.

items.title: Serian API hits ‘Very Unhealthy’ level of 241 as Sarawak air quality worsens
items.summary: The Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) in an update at 5.32pm on Thursday said dry conditions prevailed over most parts of the southern Asean region except over the northern parts of Borneo where some showers were observed. Scattered to widespread hotspots were detected in Indonesia’s Kalimantan and Sumatra, while few to isolated hotspots were detected elsewhere in the southern Asean region. “Moderate to dense smoke plumes were also observed to emanate from hotspot clusters detected in many parts of Kalimantan and the southern parts of Sumatra.

items.title: MCMC: Scammers turn to RCS, iMessage after hyperlink restrictions on SMS
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 21 — Online scams have been detected shifting to messaging services such as Rich Communication Services (RCS) and iMessage to spread phishing links following the enforcement of hyperlink restrictions on short messaging service (SMS). Selangor Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) Telecommunications Fraud deputy director Mohd Amirul Hakim Abdul Rahim said the shift was detected as these messaging services still allowed the transmission of hyperlinks to users for phishing purposes. Besides the MCMC representative, the forum featured National Financial Crime Centre (NFCC) director-general Datuk Seri Shamshun Baharin Mohd Jamil, Selangor Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) chief SAC Mohamad Rosni Mohamed Lazim and Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) LINK and Offices Department (JLPB) deputy director Hasjun Hashim as panellists.

items.title: Kuantan police corporal jailed nine months after Court of Appeal reinstates RM700 bribery conviction
items.summary: A three-judge panel, comprising Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, also upheld the Sessions Court’s order that Mohamed Syaffiq Mohamed Sidek, 36, pay a RM10,000 fine, or serve 12 months’ jail in default. The panel allowed the prosecution’s cross-appeal and dismissed Mohamed Syaffiq’s appeal against his conviction and sentence. Lawyers Datuk Sukri Mohamed, Melissa Sukri and Shahidah Muslimah Roslan represented Mohamed Syaffiq.

items.title: Sabah Immigration repatriates 4,750 undocumented migrants so far this year
items.summary: TAWAU, Aug 21 — The Sabah Immigration Department has repatriated 4,750 illegal immigrants of various nationalities to their respective countries so far this year. In a statement yesterday, the Sabah Immigration Department said Filipinos accounted for the highest number at 3,008, followed by Indonesians (1,478), Pakistanis (118), Chinese (109), Vietnamese (18) and 19 others of various nationalities. The Sabah Immigration Department urged the public to channel any information or complaints regarding illegal immigrant activities through the Public Complaints Management System (SISPAA) portal or the Online Enquiry System (SPO).

items.title: Fadhlina pushes swift investigation into alleged bullying, racial discrimination at KL school after student’s death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Schools Inspectorate, District Education Office and Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur Education Department have been directed to promptly complete an internal investigation into the alleged bullying and discrimination at a school here recently. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said matters of public concern, including those related to bullying and racial elements, must be taken seriously and addressed promptly based on facts and due processes. At the same time, Fadhlina said attention and appropriate support were also being provided to the affected families, students, teachers and the entire school community.

items.title: Penang land scandal: MACC arrests government agency chairman, four others over undervalued sales
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 21 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained five individuals, including the chairman of a government agency, for allegedly exploiting their positions in the disposal of eight plots of land in Penang. The suspects, aged between their 40s and 50s, include a chairman with a Datuk title, two company directors, a technical manager, and a clerk, TV3 reported. Sources indicate that the chairman allegedly abused his dual roles as deputy chairman and board member in 2015 to sanction the sale of eight plots of land in Seberang Perai Selatan.
